x.ASV: For the Chief Musician; on stringed instruments, set to the Sheminith. A Psalm of David. O Jehovah, rebuke me not in thine anger, Neither chasten me in thy hot displeasure.
x.Darby: To the chief Musician. On stringed instruments, upon Sheminith. A Psalm of David. Jehovah, rebuke me not in thine anger, and chasten me not in thy hot displeasure.
x.KJV: To the chief Musician on Neginoth upon Sheminith, A Psalm of David. O Lord, rebuke me not in thine anger, neither chasten me in thy hot displeasure.
x.YLT: To the Overseer with stringed instruments, on the octave. --A Psalm of David. O Jehovah, in Thine anger reprove me not, Nor in Thy fury chastise me.

nt: These two phrases mean basically the same thing. See the Introduction to this chapter for additional information on parallelism. Alternate translation: [do not rebuke or discipline me when you are angry]
Here the **nose** represents anger. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in your anger]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **rage**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [furiously]

x.ASV: Have mercy upon me, O Jehovah; for I am withered away: O Jehovah, heal me; for my bones are troubled.
x.Darby: Be gracious unto me, Jehovah, for I am withered; Jehovah, heal me, for my bones tremble.
x.KJV: Have mercy upon me, O Lord; for I am weak: O Lord, heal me; for my bones are vexed.
x.YLT: Favour me, O Jehovah, for I am weak, Heal me, O Jehovah, For troubled have been my bones,

nt: The **bones** represent the whole body. His body may have been shaking because he was sick or extremely tired. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [my whole body is shaking]

x.ASV: My soul also is sore troubled: And thou, O Jehovah, how long?
x.Darby: And my soul trembleth exceedingly: and thou, Jehovah, till how long?
x.KJV: My soul is also sore vexed: but thou, O Lord, how long?
x.YLT: And my soul hath been troubled greatly, And Thou, O Jehovah, till when?

nt: The psalmist is using the question form to request an end to his suffering. If you would not use the question form for this purpose in your language, you could translate this as a statement or an exclamation. Alternate translation: [Please, do not let this continue!]

x.ASV: Return, O Jehovah, deliver my soul: Save me for thy lovingkindness’ sake.
x.Darby: Return, Jehovah, free my soul; save me for thy loving-kindness' sake.
x.KJV: Return, O Lord, deliver my soul: oh save me for thy mercies’ sake.
x.YLT: Turn back, O Jehovah, draw out my soul, Save me for Thy kindness' sake.

nt: Here, **Turn back** refers to a change from one activity to another, in this case from anger to mercy. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a comparable expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Have mercy on me]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **covenant faithfulness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [Save me because you are faithful to your covenant]

x.ASV: For in death there is no remembrance of thee: In Sheol who shall give thee thanks?
x.Darby: For in death there is no remembrance of thee; in Sheol who shall give thanks unto thee?
x.KJV: For in death there is no remembrance of thee: in the grave who shall give thee thanks?
x.YLT: For there is not in death Thy memorial, In Sheol, who doth give thanks to Thee?

nt: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **death**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [when someone has died]
Here, **remembrance** represents praise or honor. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [praise of you]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **remembrance**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [For in death people cannot remember you]

David uses this question to emphasize that no one in Sheol thanks God. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for this purpose, you could translate this as a statement or an exclamation. Alternate translation: [No one in Sheol will give you thanks!] or [The dead cannot praise you!]

x.ASV: I am weary with my groaning; Every night make I my bed to swim; I water my couch with my tears.
x.Darby: I am wearied with my groaning; all the night make I my bed to swim; I dissolve my couch with my tears.
x.KJV: I am weary with my groaning; all the night make I my bed to swim; I water my couch with my tears.
x.YLT: I have been weary with my sighing, I meditate through all the night on my bed, With my tear my couch I waste.

nt: The author’s **groaning** represents the pain or distress that he feels. If your language does not use an abstract noun for that idea, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [I am very tired because I hurt]
These are different words for the same thing. Alternate translation: [my sleeping place … my sleeping place]
אַשְׂחֶ֣ה בְ⁠כָל־לַ֭יְלָה מִטָּתִ֑⁠י בְּ֝⁠דִמְעָתִ֗⁠י עַרְשִׂ֥⁠י אַמְסֶֽה

The psalmist says his **tears** **cause** his **bed to swim** and his **couch** to **melt** as extreme statements for emphasis. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [Every night my bed gets very wet from my many tears that make my whole couch very wet]

x.ASV: Mine eye wasteth away because of grief; It waxeth old because of all mine adversaries.
x.Darby: Mine eye wasteth away through grief; it hath grown old because of all mine oppressors.
x.KJV: Mine eye is consumed because of grief; it waxeth old because of all mine enemies.
x.YLT: Old from provocation is mine eye, It is old because of all mine adversaries,

nt: In this verse, the implied cause of the eye (vision) problems the psalmist is having is his excessive crying. You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers.

Here, **eye** represents the ability to see. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your language or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [My vision has wasted away] or [I cannot see clearly]

Here the **eye** having **wasted away** means to lose the ability to see. Your language may have a comparable expression that you could use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I have lost the ability to see well]

Here, **grief** represents crying. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [from crying] or [because I cry so much]

Here the **eye** is said to **advance** which figuratively means to grow old or weak. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a comparable expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [it weakens] or [my sight weakens]

x.ASV: Depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity; For Jehovah hath heard the voice of my weeping.
x.Darby: Depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity; for Jehovah hath heard the voice of my weeping.
x.KJV: Depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity; for the Lord hath heard the voice of my weeping.
x.YLT: Turn from me all ye workers of iniquity, For Jehovah heard the voice of my weeping,

x.ASV: Jehovah hath heard my supplication; Jehovah will receive my prayer.
x.Darby: Jehovah hath heard my supplication; Jehovah receiveth my prayer.
x.KJV: The Lord hath heard my supplication; the Lord will receive my prayer.
x.YLT: Jehovah hath heard my supplication, Jehovah my prayer receiveth.

nt: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **mercy**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [my appeal for him to be merciful]

Being willing to do what the psalmist prayed for is spoken of as if his **prayer** was something that **Yahweh accepts** from him. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Yahweh will respond to my prayer]

x.ASV: All mine enemies shall be put to shame and sore troubled: They shall turn back, they shall be put to shame suddenly.
x.Darby: All mine enemies shall be ashamed and tremble exceedingly; they will turn, they will be ashamed suddenly.
x.KJV: Let all mine enemies be ashamed and sore vexed: let them return and be ashamed suddenly.
x.YLT: Ashamed and troubled greatly are all mine enemies, They turn back--ashamed in a moment!
